page.layout: Two medallion portraits with legends at the top, centred above the text; one column of running text below them, with two entries and a printer's ornament at the foot. No margin notes.

main_text.p: ACHILLES Pelei Thessaliæ regis & Thetidis filius, Græcorum fortissimus fuit. Hic iam adultus inter Lycomedis filias, muliebri indutus ornatu latitauit, opera matris quæ hac arte cavebat ne ad bellum Troianum proficisceretur, unde nō esset reversurus. Nihilominus tamen Ulyssis astu deprehensus, ad bellum perducitur. Hic Deïdamiam Lycomedis filiam compressit, ex qua Pyrrhum sustulit: quinetiam ob ereptam sibi ab Agamemnone Briseïda, pugnare destitit, donec Patrocli amicissimi mors nunciaretur, quam Hectoris morte compensauit. Cæterùm à Paride tum demum interficitur Achilles: tandem & ipse Pyrrhus Polyxenam ad sepulchrum patris immolat. Homer.in Odyss. & Vergil.lib. Eneid.2. & Statius libr. Thebaid.1. item Dares, & Dictys Cretensis.
POLYXENA Priami & Hecubæ filia speciosissima, ad tumulum Achillis à Pyrrho eiusdem Achillis filio, interficitur, ad placandos Achillis manes. Ouidius lib.13. Metamor.

Polyxenam fertur Achilles in mœnibus Troiæ conspectam adamasse, eámque in uxorem petiuisse: Priamus annuit: in Apollinis templum conuenitur, ad ineunda pacis nuptiarúmque fœdera: verum inibi interim Achilles à Paride dolo interficitur. Vide ut supra, & Euripi. Trage.

page.notes: Two woodcut medallion portraits (Achilles in helmet; Polyxena with diadem) with legends as transcribed. Printer's ornament at the foot of the page, not text, not transcribed. Stains and show-through left out. No doubtful readings.
